findings.title: In-place filter turns nil Actions into empty slice
findings.message: Filtering in place with x.Actions[:0] mutates the backing array shared with the original slice. Callers that copy later (allowed := append(...)) are fine, but a nil Actions becomes a non-nil empty slice, which changes the wire comparison (a.Actions == nil) != (b.Actions == nil) and can produce spurious diffs. In-place filtering also corrupts any aliasing slice.
findings.suggestion: Allocate a new slice, and keep nil when there are no actions.

findings.title: Secure check bypassed when state unusable
findings.message: This check runs after the usable(s) branch. When the state is not usable it falls through to the parent class implementation, which can return the real underlying view text for a secure field. It is also not applied to the firstRectForCharacterRange or other text-returning selectors.
findings.suggestion: Check protectedText(s) before the usable(s) fallback to the parent, so protected clients never delegate to the parent.

findings.title: Secure protection lags behind client switch
findings.message: secureClient is only updated after a publish is accepted, and the native text state stays unprotected until then. Early returns in publish (for example when acknowledged<s->sequence or finish fails) leave the previous secureClient in place, so a switch to a secure client may not take effect. The old (public) text can also be exposed for a different client id, and the reverse transition retains protection incorrectly.
findings.suggestion: Make the protection check use the requested client directly for the incoming client, or apply the secure flag atomically with the client switch so it cannot lag behind.
